title: Louis Armstrong's aunt in Netto's neighborhood
summary: Netto recalls Armstrong's aunt, a midwife on his street in a mixed neighborhood, and Louis's youth and support of her rent.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: In fact, Louis Armstrong used to listen to Hardy. Is that so? Yeah. I knew Louis, Louis was kind of a nigger if he ever was one. His aunt lived about four doors from me on, on Clavin Avenue. It was a mixed neighborhood down there. Mrs. Stella Armstrong, she was a midwife. It was back in the days when they had those gals that brought in the babies. And I said, well, Joe Maselli was, I went to school with Joe. And Joe used to idolize. He tried to play Louis and everything else. But Louis was in the waif's home and in jail more often than he was out. And she's come over there one time over there. I says, how's Louis? I had Louis become famous then. And she says, you know, she says, that little nigger, she says, he's calling those tunes, his tunes. And I sang them to him when he was a baby. His aunt said that. And my stepmother told me, she says, yeah, she says, she's criticizing Louis. And Louis is giving her $15 a month. And that's her rent money. He's paying her rent money.
